issues.description: PR bundles three unrelated changes (tests, README reformat with signature change, new FAQ) into one diff
issues.detail: The stated goal is adding POST tests, but the diff also rewrites the README example (cosmetic reformatting plus a StorageError.handle signature reorder and status formatting changes) and adds an FAQ entry. Reviewers cannot cheaply separate value-changing edits from typographic ones. Split into focused commits.

issues.description: README handle() signature reordered to (req, resp, ex, params) without justification
issues.detail: The README now declares handle(req, resp, ex, params), changed from the original (ex, req, resp, params). This is an undocumented drive-by change in a PR titled about POST tests. Either justify it in the commit message with a versionchanged directive or drop it; readers copying the example verbatim will be broken.

issues.description: Switch from req.stream to req.bounded_stream in things_advanced.py is unexplained and semantically load-bearing
issues.detail: The example silently swaps req.stream.read() for req.bounded_stream.read() with no comment. These have different semantics under WSGI when Content-Length is wrong or absent, and this change is what makes the new 400 test pass. The PR description disagrees with the actual diff. Add a one-line rationale and name the contract.

issues.description: New 400 test pins an incidental implementation detail rather than a stated contract
issues.detail: resp4 expects 400 for empty body with Content-Length: 1, but this outcome exists only because of the unstated bounded_stream switch in this same PR. The invariant being tested is never named in a docstring or comment. The test pins an accident as policy instead of documenting what Falcon should do when Content-Length disagrees with the body.

issues.description: FAQ example has bad taste: nested branches, contrived handler, and assert(x == y) footgun
issues.detail: The PostTest handler uses nested if/else and fabricates the 400 behavior it claims to demonstrate, when the real lesson is one line about header overrides in simulate_post. The example also uses parenthesized assert(result.status == ...), which trains readers toward the broken assert(x, y) tuple form. Rewrite as the idiomatic code a beginner should imitate.

issues.description: Omnibus test function bundles independent cases with shared mutable state and duplicated headers
issues.detail: test_things_advanced now asserts GET, POSTs, and a malformed-length POST in one function. A failure in resp3 will mask resp4. Cases share hardcoded Authorization and Content-Type headers with no fixture. Split into named tests per invariant and extract common headers into a local dict.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. The core test additions are useful, but the PR bundles unrelated changes (tests, a README reformat with an undocumented StorageError.handle signature reorder, and a new FAQ entry) and rests on an unexplained semantic swap from req.stream to req.bounded_stream that makes the new 400 assertion pin an accident rather than a named contract. The FAQ example fabricates the behavior it claims to teach and ships taste problems (nested branches, parenthesized assert). Split the patch, name the Content-Length contract, comment the bounded_stream switch, and rewrite the FAQ example to the one line that actually demonstrates header override.
